title: Study Links Video Game Use to Problems in School
main_content:
A new study warns that too much time spent playing computer games could affect a child’s performance at school.

Britain’s National Children’s Bureau Northern Ireland reported the results of the study. They show that too many hours spent playing games can reduce students’ chances of success in school.

Earlier this month, the group’s Northern Ireland office reported the results of a study called “ICT and Me.”

The research involved more than 600 individuals between the ages of 14 and 16. It took place over a period of two years, from 2012 to 2014.

The study found that teenagers who played computer games less than once a week were more successful in school than those who played them twice a day or more.

The study found that social media use did not affect school performance.

Celine McStravick is the director of the National Children’s Bureau Northern Ireland. She says the study showed no connection between social media and test results.

Many parents say their children are becoming dependent on computer games. Some have compared gaming to a drug addiction.
